'''Steven J. Cooke''' is a Canadian biologist specializing in ecology and conservation physiology of fish. He is best known for his integrative work on fish physiology, behaviour, ecology, and human-dimensions to understand and solve complex environmental problems. He currently is a Canada Research Professor in [[Environmental science|Environmental Science]] and Biology at [[Carleton University]].  He serves as a [https://www.glfc.org/commissioners.php Canadian Commissioner] for the Great Lakes Fishery Commission and as the Editor-in-Chief of the ''[[American Fisheries Society]]'' magazine ''Fisheries'', Senior Editor of the Collaboration for Environmental Evidence journal Environmental Evidence,<ref>{{Cite web|url=https://environmentalevidencejournal.biomedcentral.com/|title=Environmental Evidence|website=BioMed Central}}</ref> and Emeritus Editor and Strategic Advisor for the journal ''[[Conservation Physiology]]''.

== Education ==
Cooke started his postsecondary education at the [[University of Waterloo]] in Ontario, Canada (1993-1999) where he attained a [[Bachelor of Environmental Studies]] and a master's in biology.<ref name=feclpSJC>{{Cite web|url=http://www.fecpl.ca/people/steven-j-cooke/|title=Steven J. Cooke|website=www.fecpl.ca|accessdate=7 June 2023}}</ref><ref name=carletonsjc>{{Cite web|url=https://carleton.ca/biology/people/steven-j-cooke/|title=Steven J. Cooke|website=carleton.ca|accessdate=7 June 2023}}</ref> Cooke completed his doctorate at the [[University of Illinois at Urbana-Champaign]] (1999-2002) with [[David Philipp (biologist)|David Philipp]] and David Wahl where he studied the physiological diversity of sunfish in the Department of Natural Resources and Environmental Sciences.<ref name=hydro>{{Cite web|url=http://www.hydronet.umontreal.ca/board_d_member_7.htm|title=NSERC HydroNet Network - The Network - Board of Directors - Member of the Board of Directors|website=www.hydronet.umontreal.ca|accessdate=7 June 2023}}</ref><ref>Cooke, S.J., P.J. Weatherhead, D.H. Wahl, and D.P. Phillip. 2008. Parental care in response to natural variation in nest predation pressure in six sunfish (Centrarchidae: Teleostei) species. Ecology of Freshwater Fish. 17(4):628-638</ref>

== Career ==

Following his Ph.D., Dr. Cooke accepted a post-doctoral position (with support from NSERC and the Killam Trust) with the Centre for Applied Conservation Research at the [[University of British Columbia]] (2002-2005) where he studied the migration biology of [[sockeye salmon]] with Dr. Scott Hinch and Dr. Tony Farrell.<ref name="hydro" /> He joined the professoriate in 2005 and now is a Full Professor of Environmental Science and Biology at [[Carleton University]].<ref name=feclpSJC /><ref name=carletonsjc /> He is also the [[Canada Research Chair]] in Fish Ecology and Conservation Physiology.<ref>[http://www.chairs-chaires.gc.ca/chairholders-titulaires/profile-eng.aspx?profileId=2579 Canada Research Chair – Profile<!-- Bot generated title -->]</ref>  His Carleton research lab consists of approximately 30 members,<ref>{{Cite web|url=http://www.fecpl.ca/people/|title=People|website=www.fecpl.ca|accessdate=7 June 2023}}</ref> including undergraduate and graduate students and post docs, and he teaches specialized courses in aquatic biology and ecology.<ref name=carletonsjc />  He has launched the careers of several prominent biologists, including Forbes 30 Under 30 Winner in Science [[Austin Gallagher|Dr. Austin Gallagher]], who was a postdoctoral fellow in his lab at the time.<ref>{{Cite web|url=https://newsroom.carleton.ca/2016/01/06/carletons-austin-gallagher-named-on-forbes-30-under-30-list/|title=Carleton's Austin Gallagher and Ben Kane on Forbes 30 Under 30 List|website=newsroom.carleton.ca|access-date=2018-02-26}}</ref> He serves as an adjunct professor in the Department of Forest and Conservation Science at the [[University of British Columbia]], an adjunct professor in the Biology Department at the [[University of Waterloo]], an affiliate at the [[Illinois Natural History Survey]]<ref>{{Cite web|url=http://wwx.inhs.illinois.edu/directory/ls/affiliate|title=INHS Directory<!-- Bot generated title -->|accessdate=7 June 2023}}</ref> and is a Special Graduate Faculty at the [[University of Illinois at Urbana-Champaign]].<ref name=feclpSJC />  In 2014 he was appointed as Director of the Institute of Environmental Science at Carleton University which became the Institute of Environmental and Interdisciplinary Science in July 2018.  Cooke held a Tier II Canada Research Chair from 2009 to 2019.

In addition to his academic activities, Dr. Cooke is the Editor-in-Chief of the [[Oxford University Press]]’s journal [[Conservation Physiology]] [https://web.archive.org/web/20130501103516/http://conphys.oxfordjournals.org/ Oxford Journals | Life Sciences | Conservation Physiology] on behalf of the [[Society for Experimental Biology]].<ref>{{Cite web|url=http://conphys.oxfordjournals.org/|title=Oxford Journals &#124; Life Sciences &#124; Conservation Physiology|date=1 May 2013|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20130501103516/http://conphys.oxfordjournals.org/ |accessdate=7 June 2023|archive-date=2013-05-01 }}</ref> He also serves on the editorial boards for FACETS, Environmental Reviews, Socio-Ecological Practice Research, and Environmental Biology of Fishes. In 2009 he published and edited a book (with Dr. [[David Philipp (biologist)|David Philipp]]) on the biology and management of centrarchid fishes titled ''Centrarchid Fishes: Diversity, Biology and Conservation''.<ref>{{Cite book|title=Centrarchid Fishes: Diversity, Biology and Conservation|editor-first1=Steven|editor-last1=Cooke|editor-first2=David P.|editor-last2=Philipp|date=15 June 2009|publisher=Wiley-Blackwell|isbn=978-1405133425 }}</ref> He was the president of the Canadian Aquatic Resources Section of the [[American Fisheries Society]]<ref>{{Cite web|url=http://www.fisheriessociety.org/cars/cars/About.html|archiveurl=https://web.archive.org/web/20131226192621/http://www.fisheriessociety.org/cars/cars/About.html|url-status=dead|title=About|archivedate=December 26, 2013|website=www.fisheriessociety.org}}</ref> from 2011-2013 and served as the Chair of the [[Sea lamprey|Sea Lamprey]] Research Board of the [[Great Lakes Fishery Commission]] from 2013-2023 before becoming Chair of their Board of Technical Experts in 2023.<ref>{{Cite web |url=http://www.glfc.org/research/slrbmem.pdf |title=Archived copy |access-date=2013-12-08 |archive-date=2013-12-27 |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20131227064754/http://www.glfc.org/research/slrbmem.pdf |url-status=dead }}</ref>  He is Past President of the International Section of the American Fisheries Society (served as president from 2017-2018) and Past President of the Society for Canadian Aquatic Sciences (served as president from 2023-2024), a society he helped found.  He was previously involved in leadership roles with NSERC HydroNet <ref name=hydro /> and [[Ocean Tracking Network]].<ref>{{Cite web|url=http://otncanada.org/people/network-investigators|archiveurl=https://web.archive.org/web/20131126154606/http://otncanada.org/people/network-investigators|url-status=dead|title=OTN Canada Network Investigators — OTN Canada<!-- Bot generated title -->|archivedate=26 November 2013|accessdate=7 June 2023}}</ref> In 2013 he delivered a TEDx talk on the future of recreational fishing.<ref>{{Cite web|url=https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=Wsz8Wn76h-4|title=Fishing for the Future: Dr. Steven Cooke at TEDxCarletonU|date=May 2013 |accessdate=7 June 2023|via=www.youtube.com}}</ref>  He is a Science Ambassador and Board Chair for KeepFishWet [https://www.keepemwet.org/ Fishing].  Cooke launched the Canadian Centre for [[Evidence-based conservation|Evidence-Based Conservation]] and Environmental Management in 2014 - an affiliate of the UK-based Collaboration for Environmental Evidence. In 2014 Cooke conceived and launched the "Legends in Canadian Fisheries Science and Management" initiative to recognize luminaries in Canadian fisheries through the Canadian Aquatic Resources Section of the American Fisheries Society.<ref>{{cite web | url=https://cars.fisheries.org/legends-of-canadian-fisheries-science-and-management/ | title=Legends &#124; Canadian Aquatic Resources Section }}</ref> As of February 2026, Dr. Cooke has published over 1200 peer-reviewed scientific papers.

== Notable awards and honours ==

In 2005, Cooke received the Award of Excellence from the [[Fisheries management|Fisheries Management]] Section of the American Fisheries Society (AFS) jointly with Drs. Scott Hinch, Tony Farrell and Mike Healey.<ref>[http://www.sdafs.org/fmsafs/awards/award-of-excellence/ Award of Excellence | Fisheries Management Section<!-- Bot generated title -->]</ref>  In 2008 he received the [[FSBI Medal]] from the Fisheries Society of the British Isles.<ref>{{Cite web|url=http://researchworks.carleton.ca/2008_October/259.htm|archiveurl=https://web.archive.org/web/20131226205032/http://researchworks.carleton.ca/2008_October/259.htm|url-status=dead|title=News briefs – October 2008 – Research Works<!-- Bot generated title -->|archivedate=26 December 2013|accessdate=7 June 2023}}</ref> In 2009 he jointly won the Distinguished Service Award from AFS.<ref>{{Cite web|url=http://fisheries.org/awards_hist|archiveurl=https://web.archive.org/web/20151004220341/http://fisheries.org/awards_hist|url-status=dead|title=Past AFS Award Winners<!-- Bot generated title -->|archivedate=4 October 2015|accessdate=7 June 2023}}</ref>  In 2013, he was selected as the J.C. Stevenson Lecturer for the [[Canadian Conference for Fisheries Research]]<ref>[http://www1.uwindsor.ca/glier/ccffr/past-programsabstracts Past Programs, Abstracts and Archives | Canadian Conference For Fisheries Research - University of Windsor<!-- Bot generated title -->]</ref> and the same year received the Roderick Haig-Brown Award from the [[Canadian Wildlife Federation]].<ref>{{Cite web|url=http://cwf-fcf.org/en/explore-our-work/funding-awards/awards/2013-roderick-haig-brown.html|archiveurl=https://web.archive.org/web/20131227011130/http://cwf-fcf.org/en/explore-our-work/funding-awards/awards/2013-roderick-haig-brown.html|url-status=dead|title=Canadian Wildlife Federation: 2013-Roderick Haig-Brown Award<!-- Bot generated title -->|archivedate=27 December 2013|accessdate=7 June 2023}}</ref>  In 2015, Cooke was named an [[NSERC]] E.W.R. Steacie Memorial Fellow.<ref>{{Cite web |url=http://science.carleton.ca/news/15/steven-cooke-and-richard-amos-receive-prestigious-nserc-awards |title=Steven Cooke and Richard Amos Receive Prestigious NSERC Awards &#124; Faculty of Science &#124; Faculty of Science - Carleton University |access-date=2015-02-21 |archive-date=2015-02-21 |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20150221060603/http://science.carleton.ca/news/15/steven-cooke-and-richard-amos-receive-prestigious-nserc-awards |url-status=dead }}</ref> Cooke is also a "Research Fellow" for Bonefish and Tarpon Trust.  In 2015 Cooke was elected into the [[Royal Society of Canada]]'s College of New Scholars, Artists, and Scientists and served as the Secretary and member of the RSC's Council (2017-2019) and was subsequently elected as a Fellow in 2022.  In 2017 Cooke became a Fellow of the [[Royal Canadian Geographical Society]] and in 2018 he was elected as a Fellow of the American Fisheries Society.<ref>{{Cite web | url=https://newsroom.carleton.ca/2018/carletons-steven-cooke-receives-fellow-award-from-the-american-fisheries-society/ | title=Carleton's Steven Cooke Receives Fellow Award from the American Fisheries Society| date=2018-08-21}}</ref>  In 2018 he was named the TD Walter Bean Visiting Professor in the Environment at the [[University of Waterloo]].<ref>{{Cite news | url=https://uwaterloo.ca/science/events/td-walter-bean-lecture-environment | title=TD Walter Bean Lecture in Environment| newspaper=Science| date=2018-09-17}}</ref>  In 2019 he was named the Robin Welcomme Fellow in Inland Fisheries at [[Michigan State University]].  In 2002-2024 Cooke was a Distinguished Presidential Scholar with the Chinese Academy of Science and during his sabbatical in 2024/2025 was a visiting scholar in the Zoology Department at Cambridge University.  Cooke was elected as a [[Fellow of the Royal Society of Canada]] in 2022. In 2021 he received the Marsh Award for Marine and Freshwater Conservation from the [[Zoological Society of London]] and in 2024 received the Conservation Award from the [[International Game Fish Association]].

== Research contributions ==
Cooke's research has contributed to many aspects of the biology, conservation and management of fish and aquatic ecosystems. One area of focus includes reproduction and fitness physiology primarily using [[centrarchid]] fish. For example, his research revealed that parental care of [[centrarchid]] fishes is energetically<ref>Cooke, S.J., D.P. Philipp, D.H. Wahl, and P.J. Weatherhead.  2006. Parental care energetics of six syntopic centrarchid fishes. Oecologia. 148:235-249.</ref><ref>Ros, A.F.H., T. Fagundes, R.F. Oliveira. 2009. Adjustment of brood size and androgen levels in a teleost with exclusive male parental care. Animal Behaviour. 78(1):25-33</ref> and physiologically<ref>Hanson, K.C., and S.J. Cooke. 2009. Nutritional condition and physiology of paternal care in two congeneric species of black bass (Micropterus spp.) relative to stage of offspring development</ref> demanding. Often, Cooke uses novel technology, like EMG transmitters<ref>Cooke S.J., E. Thorstad, S.G. Hinch. 2004. Activity and energetics of free-swimming fish: insights from electromyogram telemetry. Fish Fish 5:21-52</ref> and telemetry techniques to understand the behavior of and physiology of free-living animals. Recently he provided a framework for the application of telemetry techniques to enable [[IUCN Red List]] ranking.<ref>Cooke, S.J. 2008. Biotelemetry and biologging in endangered species research and animal conservation: relevance to regional, national, and IUCN Red List [[threat assessment]]s. Endangered Species Research 4:165-185.</ref>  Cooke uses interdisciplinary approaches (ranging from behaviour to genomics<ref>Cooke, S.J., S.G. Hinch, A.P. Farrel, D.A. Patterson, K. Miller-Saunders, D.W. Welch, M.R. Donaldson, K.C. Hanson, G.T. Crossin, I. Olsson, M.S. Cooperman, M.T. Mathes, K.A. Hruska, G.N. Wagner, R. Homason, R. Hourston, K.K. English, S. Larsson, J.M. Shrimpton, and G. Van Der Kraak. 2008. Developing a mechanistic understanding of fish migrations by linking telemetry with physiology, behaviour, genomics and experimental biology: an interdisciplinary case study on adult Fraser River sockeye salmon. Fisheries 33: 321-338.</ref>) to study complex conservation and management problems.  In particular, he has conducted basic research in support of applied problems for Pacific salmon in British Columbia.<ref>Pon, L.B., S.G. Hinch, S.J. Cooke, D.A. Patterson, and A.P. Farrell. 2009. A comparison of the physiological condition, and fishway passage time and success of migrant adult sockeye salmon at Seton River dam, British Columbia under three operational water discharge rates. North American Journal of Fisheries Management 29:1195-1205</ref> For example, his research has revealed that unsuccessful upriver adult migrants tend to be characterized by advanced reproductive development, disease, and stress, relative to those salmon that reach spawning grounds and reproduce.<ref>Cooke, S.J., S.G. Hinch, G.T. Crossin, D.A. Patterson, K.K. English, M. C. Healey. J. M. Shrimpton, G. Van Der Kraak and A. P. Farrell. 2006. Mechanistic basis of individual mortality in Pacific salmon during spawning migrations. Ecology. 87:1575-1586.</ref><ref>Young, J.L., S.G. Hinch, S.J. Cooke, G.T. Crossin, D.A. Patterson, A.P. Farrell, G. Van Der Kraak, A.G. Lotto, A. Lister, M. C. Healey, and K. K. English. 2006.  Physiological and energetic correlates of en route mortality for abnormally early migrating adult sockeye salmon (Oncorhynchus nerka) in the Thompson River, British Columbia. Canadian Journal of Fisheries and Aquatic Sciences. 63:1067-1077.</ref> This type of information has been used to influence fisheries policy in Canada <ref>{{cite web|url=http://www.pac.dfo-mpo.gc.ca/science/habitat/frw-rfo/frwbio-rfobio-eng.html |title=Fisheries and Oceans Canada &#124; Pacific Region &#124; Freshwater and Marine Habitat |publisher=Pac.dfo-mpo.gc.ca |date=2013-09-13 |accessdate=2013-12-30}}</ref> including the refinement of a management adjustment models <ref>{{Cite web|url=https://www.dfo-mpo.gc.ca/Library/331503.pdf|title=We couldn't find that Web page (Error 404) - Government of Canada Web Usability theme / Nous ne pouvons trouver cette page Web (Erreur 404) - Thème de la facilité d'emploi Web du gouvernement du Canada|website=www.dfo-mpo.gc.ca|accessdate=7 June 2023}}</ref> for harvest levels of salmon. Cooke has also been a leader in defining the emerging discipline of “conservation physiology”<ref>Wikelski M., and S.J. Cooke.  2006.  Conservation physiology.  Trends in Ecology and Evolution (Invited Contribution).  21:38-46.</ref><ref>Cooke, S.J., D.T. Blumstein, R. Buchholz, T. Caro, E. Fernández-Juricic, C.E. Franklin, J. Metcalfe, C.M. O'Connor, C. Cassidy St. Clair, W.J. Sutherland, and M. Wikelski. In Press. Physiology, behaviour and conservation.  Physiological and Biochemical Zoology 00:000-000.</ref> by developing physiological techniques that enable rapid assessment of causes of conservation problems and consequences of conservation actions. He has recently extended these ideas to the field of [[ecological restoration]].<ref>Cooke, S.J., and C.D. Suski. 2008. Ecological restoration and physiology: An overdue integration. BioScience 58: 957-968.</ref> Understanding physiology can help conservation biologists provide legislators, courts and conservation managers with the mechanisms underlying conservation problems. Cooke’s research in the domain of [[fisheries science]] focuses on sustainable fisheries which includes quantifying the consequences of fishing on fish and fisheries and developing and promoting strategies that reduce stress and increase survival through refinement of [[catch-and-release]] fishing practices.<ref>Arlinghaus, R., S.J. Cooke, J. Lyman, D. Policansky, A. Schwab, C.D. Suski, S.G. Sutton, and E.B. Thorstad. 2007. Understanding the complexity of catch-and-release in recreational fishing: an integrative synthesis of global knowledge from historical, ethical, social, and biological perspectives. Reviews in Fisheries Science. 15:75-167.</ref>  His expertise were used to co-authored the UN [[FAO]] technical guidelines for recreational fisheries in 2012.<ref>{{cite web|url=https://www.fao.org/3/i2708e/i2708e00.pdf|title=Recreational Fisheries|website=FAO|access-date=7 June 2023}}</ref> Cooke’s research has illuminated problems in recreational fishing and possible development of effective countermeasures to conserve fisheries and his work has helped to refine management strategies in Canada<ref>[http://www.mnr.gov.on.ca/stdprodconsume/groups/lr/@mnr/@letsfish/documents/document/228125.pdf Let's Fish] mnr.gov.on.ca {{Webarchive|url=https://web.archive.org/web/20131227183004/http://www.mnr.gov.on.ca/stdprodconsume/groups/lr/@mnr/@letsfish/documents/document/228125.pdf |date=2013-12-27 }}</ref> and the USA.<ref>{{Cite web|url=https://carleton.ca/biology/2013/biology-professor-receives-2013-canadian-wildlife-federation-award/|title=Biology Professor Receives 2013 Canadian Wildlife Federation Award|date=11 June 2013|website=carleton.ca|accessdate=7 June 2023}}</ref>  Cooke has also been involved in efforts to raise the profile of the threats facing [[freshwater fish]]<ref>{{Cite journal|last1=Cooke|first1=Steven J.|last2=Allison|first2=Edward H.|last3=Beard|first3=T. Douglas|last4=Arlinghaus|first4=Robert|last5=Arthington|first5=Angela H.|last6=Bartley|first6=Devin M.|last7=Cowx|first7=Ian G.|last8=Fuentevilla|first8=Carlos|last9=Leonard|first9=Nancy J.|date=2016-11-01|title=On the sustainability of inland fisheries: Finding a future for the forgotten|journal=Ambio|volume=45|issue=7|pages=753–764|doi=10.1007/s13280-016-0787-4|issn=1654-7209|pmc=5055481|pmid=27312662|bibcode=2016Ambio..45..753C }}</ref> and freshwater biodiversity more broadly.<ref>{{Cite journal|last1=Reid|first1=Andrea J.|last2=Carlson|first2=Andrew K.|last3=Creed|first3=Irena F.|last4=Eliason|first4=Erika J.|last5=Gell|first5=Peter A.|last6=Johnson|first6=Pieter T. J.|last7=Kidd|first7=Karen A.|last8=MacCormack|first8=Tyson J.|last9=Olden|first9=Julian D.|title=Emerging threats and persistent conservation challenges for freshwater biodiversity|journal=Biological Reviews|issue=3|pages=849–873|doi=10.1111/brv.12480|pmid=30467930|issn=1469-185X|year=2018|volume=94|doi-access=free}}</ref>  He reflects on his successes and failures in generating management- and policy-relevant science in a reflective essay.<ref>{{Cite journal |doi = 10.1007/s42532-018-0002-x|title = From frustration to fruition in applied conservation research and practice: Ten revelations|journal = Socio-Ecological Practice Research|volume = 1|pages = 15–23|year = 2019|last1 = Cooke|first1 = Steven J.| issue=1 |doi-access = | bibcode=2019SEPR....1...15C }}</ref>
